note.text: Détente means an easing of international tension through negotiation and practical accommodation. In Cold War study it commonly refers to improved US-Soviet relations, especially in the late 1960s and 1970s. Fear of nuclear escalation, the costs of competition and strategic calculations encouraged talks. Détente did not erase ideological differences, alliances or conflicts elsewhere. Arms limitation controlled specified weapons or systems; it was not the destruction of every weapon. A temporary easing must be distinguished from a permanent settlement.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to recognise negotiated reductions in tension and distinguish arms limitation from disarmament or the end of the Cold War. Builds on: Cold War rivalry, alliances and nuclear risk. Leads to: assessing agreements and the continued choices of states during decolonisation.

sections.heading: Explain the history
sections.text: Détente means an easing of international tension through negotiation and practical accommodation. In Cold War study it commonly refers to improved US-Soviet relations, especially in the late {1960}s and {1970}s. Fear of nuclear escalation, the costs of competition and strategic calculations encouraged talks. Détente did not erase ideological differences, alliances or conflicts elsewhere. Arms limitation controlled specified weapons or systems; it was not the destruction of every weapon. A temporary easing must be distinguished from a permanent settlement.

sections.heading: Follow the evidence and examples
sections.text: The Limited Test Ban Treaty of {1963} was an earlier step towards controlling nuclear danger; it did not ban all underground testing. SALT agreements in {1972} included the ABM Treaty and an interim limit on specified strategic offensive weapons. The Helsinki Final Act in {1975} addressed European security, cooperation and human rights. Meetings, exchanges and agreements offered channels for managing rivalry. Continued intervention and renewed tension, notably around the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in {1979}, show the limits of accommodation.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Ask what an agreement actually covers: testing, launchers, defensive systems or diplomatic principles. Compare obligations with implementation and later events. A photograph of leaders meeting proves contact, not complete agreement. Do not confuse the date of signing with ratification or enforcement. Explain both what changed and which rivalries continued.

cards.idea: Check a claim against the sequence, setting and limits of the evidence.
example: Détente means every political disagreement and conflict has ended permanently. Correction: Accommodation can reduce tension without eliminating the underlying rivalry.
A limit on specified systems means all weapons everywhere were destroyed. Correction: Scope matters: partial limits are different from universal disarmament.
The Helsinki Final Act was the agreement founding NATO in {1949}. Correction: Helsinki belonged to a later effort at cooperation, not NATO’s founding.
One summit guaranteed that no later crisis could occur. Correction: Later crises demonstrate that negotiated easing was conditional and reversible.
